name: Kramskoi Voronezh Regional Art Museum
overview: Regional art museum at Prospekt Revolyutsii 18 in Voronezh (address in the footer of the museum's site), in a Baroque building of 1777 to 1779 designed by the architect N. N. Ievsky, listed as a monument of federal significance (stated by the museum; museum.ru).

Created in 1933 as the Museum of Fine Arts from the collections of the Provincial Museum and the Museum of Antiquities and Fine Arts of Voronezh University. It has carried the name of the painter Ivan Kramskoi since 1984 (stated by the museum).

The building's first owner was the Voronezh governor I. A. Potapov. It passed to the Voronezh Provincial Museum in 1911, has housed the art museum since 1947, was restored in 1952 and 1953 after wartime fire damage, and gained an exhibition hall in 1984 (stated by the museum).
funding_verdict: Kramskoi Voronezh Regional Art Museum: public: a regional state museum founded by the Voronezh Region Ministry of Culture, with ticket and service income

name: Yekaterinburg Museum of Fine Arts
overview: Municipal art museum with five sites in Yekaterinburg: the main building at 5 Voevodina Street, the Hermitage-Ural cultural centre at 11 Vainera Street, the Museum of Naive Art, the Stone-Carving History Center named after A. K. Denisov-Uralsky, and a restoration and storage centre at 16A Vainera Street (museum website).

Founded on 1 April 1936 and registered as a municipal autonomous cultural institution on 3 December 2015. The founder is the Department of Culture of the Yekaterinburg city administration and the director is Nikita Nikolayevich Korytin (museum website).
Former names: Wikipedia gives the Sverdlovsk Art Gallery as the museum's original gallery, and says it took its current name in 1992 and gained full museum status in 1988.
funding_verdict: Yekaterinburg Museum of Fine Arts: public: Yekaterinburg city administration as founder, with regional and federal money for Hermitage-Ural

name: Hayy Jameel
overview: Arts and creative complex of 17,000 square metres in the Al Muhammadiyah district of Jeddah, developed and managed by Art Jameel (ArtAsiaPacific, hayyjameel.org).

Opened to the public on 6 December 2021 after an opening first slated for late 2020. The launch marked 75 years of Jameel family philanthropy (Arab News, ArtAsiaPacific, Abdul Latif Jameel press release).
"Hayy" is the Arabic word for neighbourhood (hayyjameel.org).
funding_verdict: Hayy Jameel: private family philanthropy: Art Jameel, founded by Fady Jameel

name: National Museum of Singapore
overview: Singapore's national history museum at 93 Stamford Road.
Established in 1849 by the Singapore Institution Committee as the Raffles Library and Museum, a section of a library at the Singapore Institution (Wikipedia).
It moved to Stamford Road in 1887, into a building designed by Henry McCallum and built in a scaled-down version by J. F. McNair.
funding_verdict: National Museum of Singapore: public: the National Heritage Board and its parent ministry

name: STPI Creative Workshop & Gallery
overview: Print and paper workshop and contemporary art gallery at 41 Robertson Quay, by the Singapore River (Wikipedia; Little Day Out).

Formed in 2002 as the Singapore Tyler Print Institute in line with the Singapore government's Renaissance City Plan, which e-flux (6 January 2017) ties to making Singapore a leading arts centre in Southeast Asia. Deputy Prime Minister Tony Tan opened it on 10 April 2002 (Wikipedia).

The American master printer Kenneth E. Tyler's equipment and expertise moved to Singapore. The presses were shipped from his New York studio and a paper mill was installed (Wikipedia, which credits Renaissance City Plan director Liu Thai Ker with persuading him).
funding_verdict: STPI: non-profit supported by donors and patrons and "various funding sources" (STPI website)

name: Kapelica Gallery (Kersnikova Institute)
overview: Gallery for contemporary and research-based art at Likozarjeva ulica 1, Ljubljana (culture.si portal).
Established in 1995 by the Student Organisation of the University of Ljubljana (ŠOU) and led since then by the architect and curator Jurij Krpan (culture.si).
Named after a former chapel (kapelica) at Kersnikova 4, its earlier premises (culture.si).
funding_verdict: Kapelica Gallery (Kersnikova Institute): mainly public: EU programmes, the Slovenian Ministry of Culture and the City of Ljubljana

name: MGLC International Centre of Graphic Arts
overview: Museum of fine art prints, contemporary art gallery and print publisher with its own printmaking workshops, in Tivoli Mansion in Tivoli Park, Ljubljana. Its address is Pod turnom 3 (Visit Ljubljana, MGLC).

Established as a public institute by the City of Ljubljana through a decree adopted by the city council on 15 April 1999 and published in Uradni list RS 42/1999 (3 June 1999). It produces the Ljubljana Biennale of Graphic Arts, which began in 1955 (Uradni list, Visit Ljubljana).

The decree (Article 3) lists its activities: the international graphic biennial, domestic and foreign exhibitions, a permanent exhibition of modern Slovenian and foreign graphics, an experimental graphics workshop, publishing and symposia.
funding_verdict: MGLC International Centre of Graphic Arts: public institute of the City of Ljubljana, founded and budgeted by the city

name: Solomon Islands National Museum
overview: National museum in Honiara with several buildings, each with a gallery on themes such as inter-island politics and independence, plus offices and an auditorium with an outdoor stage (Wikipedia).

Origins: the nucleus of an Ethnology and Natural History Museum collection was formed in 1952 and a building erected in 1953 (Solomon Islands Historical Encyclopaedia). The museum opened on 6 June 1969 and was included in the new Information, Broadcasting, Museum and Library Services department in 1972 (Solomon Islands Historical Encyclopaedia).

Building: the first stage of the modern museum was built in 1968 in Coronation Gardens, opposite the Mendana Hotel, with a grant from the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation in Lisbon (Solomon Islands Historical Encyclopaedia). The Japanese Government built the museum library in 1999 (Ministry of Culture and Tourism press release, 2022).
funding_verdict: Solomon Islands National Museum: government department with foreign aid for buildings and digitisation

name: Origins Centre
overview: Museum of human origins of the University of the Witwatersrand (Wits) in Braamfontein, Johannesburg, on a site above the M1 highway across the road from Braamfontein cemetery (Wits; Mail & Guardian, 13 April 2006).
Opened by President Thabo Mbeki in 2006 (Wits).
Built where the fine art department had its studios, known as "The Wedge" (Mail & Guardian, 2006).
funding_verdict: Origins Centre: university museum: Wits, with renovation money from a national humanities institute and the French Institute

press_items.outlet: Archive and Public Culture Research Initiative, University of Cape Town
press_items.title: John Wright, "Conversations about Art, Objects and Archives" (2019)

name: Wits Art Museum
overview: University art museum on the corner of Bertha and Jorissen Streets in Braamfontein, near the Nelson Mandela Bridge, within the University of the Witwatersrand's cultural precinct (Wits).

The collection began as a teaching collection in the early 1950s, started by Professors Heather Martienssen and John Fassler of the Architecture Department. The Gertrude Posel Gallery was established in Senate House in 1977, named in recognition of Posel's contribution to its establishment (Wits). The Mail & Guardian described the museum's new building on 18 May 2012 (Mail & Guardian).
Named for the university, the University of the Witwatersrand. Its core gallery keeps the name Gertrude Posel Gallery (Mail & Guardian).
funding_verdict: Wits Art Museum: university museum: the University of the Witwatersrand, private donors and Standard Bank as collection partner

name: Busan Museum of Art
overview: Municipal art museum at APEC-ro 58, Haeundae-gu, Busan. Hankyung calls it the Busan Municipal Museum of Art (부산시립미술관).
Reopened in September 2026 after a three-year renovation costing 46.9 billion won (Hankyung, 28 September 2026).
The reopening exhibition "Dear All The Yesterdays" runs from 17 September 2026 to 14 March 2027 and features the museum's collection (Busan Metropolitan City).
funding_verdict: Busan Museum of Art: public: municipal museum

press_items.title: Sung Su-young, "[취재수첩] 편파 전시 논란 자초한 부산시립미술관" (28 September 2026; my translation: [Reporter's Notebook] Busan Municipal Museum of Art invites controversy with a biased exhibition)

name: Amorepacific Museum of Art
overview: Corporate art museum in the Amorepacific headquarters at Hangang-daero 100, Yongsan-gu, Seoul (museum site), David Chipperfield's "luminous cube" (W Magazine, 27 August 2025).

Founded in 1979 on the art collected by Amorepacific's founder Suh Sung-whan (서성환), opening as a cosmetics museum in Daebang-dong; renamed Pacific Museum (태평양박물관) in 1997 and moved to Yongin, The Amore Museum in 2005 and Amorepacific Museum of Art in 2009, and reopened in Yongsan in 2018 (Encyclopedia of Korean Culture).
It collects Korean historical art and Korean and international contemporary art, and supports researchers, scholarly societies and young artists (Encyclopedia of Korean Culture).
funding_verdict: Amorepacific Museum of Art: corporate-owned: Amorepacific Corp., a cosmetics company
wider_context: The Korea Fair Trade Commission fined Amorepacific 500 million won in August 2014 for forcing door-to-door sales agencies to move about 3,480 high-performing sales staff to new or struggling agencies from 2005 to June 2013; the commission said this was the highest fine it could impose (Korea JoongAng Daily, 18 August 2014).

In April 2020 the commission fined Amorepacific Group and its affiliate Cosvision 48 million won each, 96 million won in all, over 75 billion won in fee-free fixed deposits that let Cosvision take five low-interest Korea Development Bank loans worth 60 billion won; the article also prints 9.6 billion won, at odds with its headline (Korea Times).
Both cases concern the museum's owner, not the museum.

name: Arario Museum in Space
overview: Private contemporary art museum at 83 Yulgok-ro, Jongno-gu, Seoul, reached from Anguk Station (Line 3, exit 3) (Time Out). Attractions Management says it overlooks Changgyeong Palace.

Founded by the collector and businessman Kim Chang-il, who also makes art as "CI Kim". The museum opened in 2014 with an inaugural show from his collection of over 200 works by 43 international artists (Attractions Management, 24 Sep 2014).

Housed in an office building designed by Kim Swoo-geun and built in 1971, once the home of his Space Group firm. The original structure was left almost untouched in the conversion (Time Out; Attractions Management).
funding_verdict: Arario Museum in Space: self-funded: the founder's Arario Group businesses
wider_context: The Korea Herald (Park Yuna, 1 Feb 2021) reported that the Daejeon District Court sentenced Kim Chang-il to two years in jail for breach of duty over the operation of a cinema concession stand at the Cheonan Bus Terminal, which the group owns. An Arario Group official said the group would file an appeal.

Chungnam Ilbo (Cha Ji-hyun, 28 Jan 2021) reported the ruling by the Cheonan branch of the Daejeon District Court and names the defendants only as A, 70, the Cheonan Arario representative (two years), and his son B, 41, the vice chairman (18 months). It says the concession stand was operated by the son's company from 2011 to 2019 and that double contracts on store leases from 2009 to 2016 cost the company 790 million won; it adds that the court noted the double-contract losses had been repaid (translated from the Korean).
The museum site names Arario Co. as its operator, and the case concerns a property of the group Kim chairs.

name: Fundació Antoni Tàpies
overview: Museum and foundation at Carrer d'Aragó 255 in Barcelona, in the former Editorial Montaner y Simón building by Lluís Domènech i Montaner (Museu Tàpies).
Created in 1984 by the painter Antoni Tàpies to advance knowledge of modern and contemporary art, and opened in June 1990 (Museu Tàpies).
Named for its founder. It holds one of the most complete collections of his work, mostly made up of donations by Antoni and Teresa Tàpies (Museu Tàpies).
funding_verdict: Fundació Antoni Tàpies: private foundation with public subsidies of 1.41 million euros in 2021 and 2.76 million euros in 2025 from the Generalitat de Catalunya, the Barcelona city council, the Spanish Ministry of Culture and the Diputació de Barcelona

name: LABoral Centro de Arte y Creación Industrial
overview: Art centre at Los Prados 121, Gijón (LABoral website).
Created in 2007 and occupying about 14,000 square metres of the former Universidad Laboral. The 2017 article credits Rosina Gómez Baeza with the initiative (elDiario.es, J.M. Costa, 2 February 2017).

Run by Fundación La Laboral. Centro de Arte, Creación Industrial y Promoción Cultural, a public cultural entity declared of general interest. Its purpose in the statutes is "the promotion and dissemination of art and industrial creation" through the centre (LABoral website).
funding_verdict: LABoral: mainly public: the Principality of Asturias, Gijón City Council and the Port Authority of Gijón

press_items.title: J.M. Costa, "Estalla el primer conflicto LABoral en un centro de arte contemporáneo" (25 February 2016)
J.M. Costa, "LABoral de Gijón, del mayor lujo a la más absoluta miseria en los centros de arte" (2 February 2017)

name: Chillida Leku
overview: Private museum and sculpture park devoted to the Basque sculptor Eduardo Chillida (1924 to 2002), around the Zabalaga farmhouse in Hernani, about 10 km from San Sebastián (Arquitectura Viva; The Art Newspaper places the museum near Hernani).
Chillida and his wife Pilar Belzunce founded it in 2000 in a converted 16th-century farmhouse (The Art Newspaper). Onda Vasca states that the land of the Zabalaga farmhouse was acquired in 1983.
"Leku" is the Basque word for "place" (Elephant, Joe Lloyd, 26 May 2020).
funding_verdict: Chillida Leku: private: the Chillida family with financial support from the gallery Hauser & Wirth

name: Es Baluard Museu
overview: Museum of modern and contemporary art at Plaça Porta Santa Catalina 10, Palma, on the perimeter of the bastion of Sant Pere, part of the Renaissance walled enclosure (the museum's history page).

Inaugurated on 30 January 2004 by the King and Queen of Spain. Palma City Council ceded the site in 1997. A foundation runs it, made up of the Balearic government, the Consell de Mallorca, Palma City Council and the Fundació d'Art Serra (the museum's organisation page).
Pere A. Serra Bauzà is listed as the board's Founding President. The Fundació d'Art Serra and Serra Bauzà donated or deposited works in the collection (the museum's organisation page).
funding_verdict: Es Baluard Museu: mainly public: Balearic government, Palma City Council and the Consell de Mallorca, with a smaller grant from Spain's Ministry of Culture

name: Artium Museoa
overview: Basque Museum Centre of Contemporary Art at C/ Francia 24, Vitoria-Gasteiz (Álava tourism board).

Opened on 26 April 2002 (Álava tourism board). The Diputación Foral de Álava, the provincial council, created the managing foundation as its sole founder: the foundation was constituted by public deed on 16 February 2001 under Foral Decree 112/2000 of 14 November 2000 (Basque Government public-sector register, 2023).
Wikipedia says the museum occupies a former bus station and names José Luis Caton as architect.
funding_verdict: Artium Museoa: mainly public, run by a foundation the Álava provincial council founded and holds as sole capital contributor

name: Colomboscope
overview: Contemporary arts festival and creative platform for interdisciplinary dialogue in Colombo, held in key historic sites of the city and running since 2013 (Colomboscope website).

Founded in 2013 by EUNIC Sri Lanka, made up of the Goethe-Institut, the British Council and the Alliance Française de Kotte. The first edition was a small event at Park Street Mews, in the slot left open when the Galle Literary Festival was postponed (Shamalee De Silva-Parizeau, "Five years of art, culture and creative wonder", Daily FT, 26 August 2017).

The 2013 edition was "Identities". Later editions included "Making history" (2014), "Testing Grounds" at the General Post Office (2016, curated by Susanne Jaschko) and "Re/evolution" (2017), the first organised by a local team (Daily FT, 2017).
funding_verdict: Colomboscope: mixed: European cultural institutes, past corporate title sponsors and individual Friends

name: Sudan National Museum
overview: Sudan's largest museum, on El Neel (Nile) Avenue in Khartoum's al-Mugran area, close to the meeting of the White and Blue Nile.
The building dates from 1955 and it became a national museum in 1971 (Wikipedia).
Run by the National Corporation for Antiquities and Museums (NCAM).
funding_verdict: Sudan National Museum: public and donor-funded: the Sudanese state through NCAM, with Italian money through UNESCO
wider_context: AP reporters found the halls trashed in April 2025; NCAM official Gamal ElDeen Zain al-Abdeen said looters broke into the storerooms and took all the gold artefacts.
Authorities blame the Rapid Support Forces, which held that district for most of the war. The force neither funds nor controls the museum.
National authorities have recovered 570 objects stolen from the museum (UN in Sudan).
The French archaeological unit SFDAS, with the Louvre and Durham University, built a virtual site to show the lost objects (Wikipedia).
